options.content: **04 · Structured values.** The grpc-go client stores `Person` protobuf messages packed in `google.protobuf.Any` and queries their fields with OQL, which works because gfsh-init deployed their descriptor JAR. Load comes from `make select-load-test EX=04 SCRIPT=people/steady`: `get` and `put` (one RPC each) plus three field queries, `by-city`, `age-range` and `nickname` (the **op** dropdown).

panels.title: At a glance: selected load runs over the time range
Peak req/s
panels.description: Computed over the whole time range for the runs picked in the "load run" dropdown, so the panel keeps its numbers after a run ends. Highest requests/s k6 sustained (30-second windows): Gets, Puts and queries.

panels.title: Peak rows/s
panels.description: Computed over the whole time range for the runs picked in the "load run" dropdown, so the panel keeps its numbers after a run ends. Highest rows/s the queries returned (30-second windows).

panels.title: GemFire call p50
panels.description: Computed over the whole time range for the runs picked in the "load run" dropdown, so the panel keeps its numbers after a run ends. Median time of the GemFire call: a Get, a Put, or a whole Query stream.

panels.title: GemFire call p99
panels.description: Computed over the whole time range for the runs picked in the "load run" dropdown, so the panel keeps its numbers after a run ends. 99th percentile.

panels.title: Failed calls
panels.description: Share of calls that failed, from the client's demo_op_latency_seconds{code!="OK"}. It counts every caller (k6, the demo, curl), so it ignores the dropdowns.

panels.title: GemFire call p50 and p99, by op
panels.description: The GemFire call as the client timed it (X-GemFire-Micros): one Get or Put RPC, or a whole Query stream. The field queries scan every Person, unpacking each one.

panels.title: Rows/s, by query
panels.description: Rows the field queries returned per second. by-city returns about 1,000 rows, age-range one (a COUNT), nickname about 2,000.

panels.title: Per op, over the time range
panels.description: Calls, average rows per call (queries only), and the GemFire call's p50/p99 for the selected runs.

targets.expr: sum by (op) (increase(k6_query_rows_total{client="grpc-go", run=~"$run", op=~"$op"}[$__range])) / sum by (op) (increase(k6_http_reqs_total{client="grpc-go", run=~"$run", op=~"$op"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Load test (k6): end-to-end vs. GemFire call
End-to-end vs. GemFire call (p50)
panels.description: The gap is the HTTP request around the call: k6 → client and back, protojson encoding.

panels.title: gRPC calls (interceptors): every call, the demo's included
gRPC calls/s by method and status code
panels.description: From the client's interceptors. Query errors (UNIMPLEMENTED for UNDEFINED, FAILED_PRECONDITION for an unregistered type, INTERNAL for an index out of bounds) come from the demo and from curl.

panels.title: QueryResponse messages per call
panels.description: About rows ÷ query-batch-size, and never less than 1: an empty result is still one message.

panels.title: GemFire servers: what the cluster sees
Region gets and puts/s per server (/people)
panels.description: PartitionedRegionStats on /people. The Any bytes are stored as they are, so a Get or Put costs the same as for any other value of that size.

panels.title: Query executions/s per server
panels.description: CachePerfStats.queryExecutions. On a partitioned region every query runs on both servers (each on its own buckets), so both count it, not only server1.

panels.title: Average execution time per server
panels.description: CachePerfStats.queryExecutionTime (nanoseconds) ÷ queryExecutions: the server's share of a query, which includes unpacking every Person to read its fields.

panels.title: Partitioned-query messages sent
panels.description: QueryMessages a server sends to the other server, asking it to run the query on its own buckets. The gRPC client talks only to server1, so server1 sends them.
